## Bug

The `databasePassword` (and `databaseRootPassword`, `password`) fields across `libsql-create`, `mariadb-create`, `mongo-create`, `mysql-create`, `postgres-create`, and their `password`\-change counterparts use a Zod `.regex()` pattern that produces an invalid JSON Schema regex. DeepSeek API's schema validator rejects it with:

```
Error from provider (DeepSeek): Invalid schema for function 'dokploy_libsql-create': "^[a-zA-Z0-9@#%^&*()_+\-=[\]{}|;:,.<>?~\`]*$" is not a "regex"
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure @dokploy/mcp with DeepSeek as the LLM provider
2. The MCP server sends tools/list to DeepSeek
3. DeepSeek rejects the schema because the `pattern` regex is not valid ECMA-262

### Root Cause

The regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9@#%^&*()_+=[\]{}|;:,.<>?~`\-\]\*$`(or its zod-to-json-schema-transformed variant) contains characters that DeepSeek's JSON Schema validator does not accept as a valid regex. Likely the backtick or how zod-to-json-schema escapes the`\-\` inside the character class.

### Affected Tools

All tools with `databasePassword`, `databaseRootPassword`, or `password` fields using this regex:

- `libsql-create`, `libsql-update`
- `mariadb-create`, `mariadb-update`, `mariadb-changePassword`
- `mongo-create`, `mongo-update`, `mongo-changePassword`
- `mysql-create`, `mysql-update`, `mysql-changePassword`
- `postgres-create`, `postgres-update`, `postgres-changePassword`
- `redis-changePassword`

### Expected Behavior

All database-related tools should register successfully with any provider that validates JSON Schema patterns (DeepSeek, Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.).

### Suggested Fix

Replace the `.regex()` constraint with a simpler validation or remove it entirely — the server validates the password anyway. For example, use `z.string().min(1)` instead of `z.string().regex(...)`.

## Summary

`@dokploy/mcp@0.29.14` (current `latest` and the only version on npm) exposes a tool schema whose  
`pattern` is rejected by strict provider-side JSON Schema validators, making **every** tool call fail  
for affected models:

```
invalid_request_error: Invalid schema for function 'dokploy_libsql-create':
"^[a-zA-Z0-9@#%^&*()_+\-=[\]{}|;:,.<>?~\`]*$" is not a "regex"
```

The root cause is an **unescaped `[` inside a character class** (`...+\-=[\]{}...`). JavaScript  
treats it as a literal, so the MCP server itself is happy — but Go/Rust `regex` engines reject it as  
ambiguous with nested classes.

**The fix already exists in `main`** (`117fe9d` — "fix: strip unsupported regex patterns from tool  
schemas", `stripUnsupportedRegexPatterns` in `src/server.ts`), **but it has never been released.**

## Why this still affects users

```
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 117fe9d v0.29.14 && echo in-release || echo NOT-in-release
NOT-in-release

$ git tag --contains 117fe9d          # no output — no tag contains it
$ git show v0.29.14:src/server.ts | grep -c usesUnsupportedRegexSyntax
0

$ npm view @dokploy/mcp dist-tags
{ "latest": "0.29.14" }               # published 2026-08-06
```

The commit's author date (2026-07-05) *looks* older than the 0.29.14 bump (2026-08-06), which makes  
this easy to miss — but it is not an ancestor of the tag, and no tag contains it. Anyone installing  
via `npx -y @dokploy/mcp` gets the unsanitized schemas.

Confirmed against the published tarball:

```
$ grep -c usesUnsupportedRegexSyntax node_modules/@dokploy/mcp/build/server.js
0
```

## Reproduction

Any OpenAI-compatible gateway forwarding `tools` to a strict provider. Minimal request:

```shell
curl -s "$GATEWAY/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "<strict-model>",
  "max_tokens": 16,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {
    "name": "dokploy_libsql-create",
    "parameters": {"type": "object",
      "properties": {"databasePassword": {"type": "string",
        "pattern": "^[a-zA-Z0-9@#%^&*()_+\-=[\]{}|;:,.<>?~\`]*$"}},
      "required": ["databasePassword"]}}}]}'
```

I bisected 12 candidate patterns to isolate the offending character. Only the bare `[` fails —  
`\-`, `\]`, `` ` ``, `{}`, `|` and lookaheads all pass.

| Provider backend | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Anthropic (opus / sonnet / haiku) | ✅ accepted |
| DeepSeek | ❌ `is not a "regex"` |
| xAI (grok-4) | ❌ `Schema validation failed: [standard_violation] /properties/databasePassword/pattern` |

After escaping to `=\[\]`, the same request succeeds on both DeepSeek and xAI. The escaped form is  
semantically identical — I verified acceptance is byte-for-byte equal across all 95 printable ASCII  
characters.

## Secondary: the `v`\-flag heuristic over-strips

`usesUnsupportedRegexSyntax()` uses `new RegExp(pattern, "v")` as the compatibility test. The `v`  
(unicodeSets) flag additionally reserves `( ) [ ] { } / - \ |` inside classes, so it rejects many  
patterns that providers accept — notably a **bare trailing `-`**, as in `^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`.

Replaying the exact `main` logic against the 0.29.14 tool set:

```
patterns: 10 distinct / 85 occurrences
stripped: 66 occurrences (8 of 10 distinct)
kept:     19 occurrences
```

Stripped patterns include:

```
x20  ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$
x 8  ^[a-zA-Z0-9 ._-]{0,500}$
x 5  ^[a-zA-Z0-9._\-/#]+$
x 3  ^--[a-zA-Z0-9-]+(=[a-zA-Z0-9._:/@-]+)?$
x 2  ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$
x 2  ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$
```

I sent all 7 of those to a strict provider (xAI) in a single request: **all accepted.** So the  
current heuristic discards useful validation on ~78% of pattern occurrences to fix one genuinely  
broken pattern.

Worth noting the escaped form (`=\[\]`) *also* fails the `v` test — because of the unescaped  
`{`, `}`, `|` — yet is accepted by every provider I tested. The `v` flag is a proxy for provider  
strictness, not a match for it.

A narrower test would preserve validation:

```ts
function usesUnsupportedRegexSyntax(pattern: unknown): boolean {
  if (typeof pattern !== "string") return false;
  if (/\(\?<?[=!]/.test(pattern)) return true;   // lookarounds
  try { new RegExp(pattern, "u"); } catch { return true; }  // must be valid ECMA-262
  return hasUnescapedOpenBracketInClass(pattern); // the actual offender
}
```

1. **Publish a release containing `117fe9d`** — this alone unblocks everyone on npm. The pinned  
	`pattern` in `openapi.json` (19 occurrences) can also simply be escaped to `=\[\]`, which is a  
	no-op in JS and valid everywhere.
2. Optionally narrow the sanitizer so it stops discarding provider-safe patterns.

## Workaround for others hitting this

Escape the bracket in the generated build (idempotent):

```shell
node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),f="node_modules/@dokploy/mcp/build/generated/tools.js";

const s=fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8");
fs.writeFileSync(f, s.split(a).join(b));
console.log("fixed:", s.split(a).length-1);'

resolves from its own cache.

## Conclusion

**Factory’s public MCP docs do not document a separate regex dialect or an MCP-to-function schema compatibility matrix.** They say Droid loads the tools a server reports, while `disabledTools` prevents selected tools from being registered. <citation refs="aamBC4WIMNMGR1xNMF1z7">“Every tool the server reports is loaded except the listed names, and excluded tools are never registered with the model.”</citation>

MCP itself carries each tool’s `inputSchema` as JSON Schema. <citation refs="jrU3BkwsdH_4g4rGngMqw">The MCP tool definition lists `inputSchema` as “JSON Schema defining expected parameters.”</citation> JSON Schema recommends ECMAScript/ECMA-262 regex semantics with Unicode support, but also warns that full syntax is not widely supported. <citation refs="X0bPPdmn6Uq8GK9UVsqCj">“The regular expression syntax used is from JavaScript (ECMA 262)… [but] that complete syntax is not widely supported.”</citation>

So this is a **provider-facing conversion/validation compatibility issue**, not proof that the MCP tool’s JSON Schema is intrinsically invalid.

- `\p{L}` and `\p{N}` are valid ECMAScript Unicode property escapes only in Unicode-aware (`u` or `v`) regex mode. `\p{L}` specifically means the Unicode Letter category. <citation refs="LrqJ8SW73hEWz8wE2kqf1">MDN states that `\p`/`\P` are only supported in Unicode-aware mode and identifies `\p{L}` as the short alias for Letter.</citation>
- A JSON Schema `pattern` is only a string and does not carry regex flags. A client/provider must choose the Unicode-aware behavior. That is a portability problem in practice.
- **Yes, strict OpenAI/Azure-compatible function-schema validators demonstrably reject this exact class of Unicode escapes.** A public Zed issue reproduces the same failure with:
  ```json
  "pattern": "^[\p{L}\p{N}_. ()-]+$"
  ```
  and the response:
  ```text
  Invalid schema for function 'createScoreConfig':
  '^[\p{L}\p{N}_. ()-]+$' is not a 'regex'
  ```
  <citation refs="jz45M_UeYjDqKhz-igyXG">The issue attributes the rejection to OpenAI/Azure-compatible provider validation of `tools[].function.parameters`, before inference.</citation>

Your Factory error:

```text
400 Invalid schema for function 'Skillplane___skills_search':
'^[\p{L}\p{N}._:-]+$' is not a 'regex'
```

matches that known **MCP-to-strict-provider function-schema** failure mode almost exactly. The evidence supports:

1. Factory is passing the MCP tool schema into a stricter downstream function/tool schema validator.
2. That validator does **not** accept `\p{L}` / `\p{N}` in this schema context.
3. Factory’s public docs do not currently promise that it normalizes such patterns or supports all ECMA-262 Unicode regex features.

I found no public Factory-AI GitHub issue containing `Skillplane___skills_search`; GitHub’s issue search returned zero results for that exact tool name. <citation refs="w65J9Kyss1IvywW6QkO2b">GitHub search reports “Issues (0)” for the exact quoted tool identifier.</citation>

### Practical compatibility conclusion

For broad MCP client/provider compatibility, the tool should avoid Unicode-property escapes in the schema it exposes to models. If Unicode validation is required, validate it inside the MCP server and either:

- omit `pattern` from the model-facing schema, or
- use an ASCII-only compatible pattern such as `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$` only if that narrower behavior is acceptable.

This keeps server-side validation authoritative while avoiding a whole tool catalog being rejected by the downstream provider.[0m

content.text:
This is a tool-registration failure, not a failure while searching Skillplane or accessing PR #8.

Skillplane exposes this validation rule for `skills_search.tags[]`:

```regex
^[\p{L}\p{N}._:-]+$
```

It comes directly from [search.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane/packages/mcp-schema/src/search.ts:28). `\p{L}` and `\p{N}` are Unicode character-property escapes. They are valid Unicode-aware JavaScript regex syntax, but Skillplane converts the Zod schema to JSON Schema in [server.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane/mcp/src/server.ts:125), where the JavaScript `u` flag cannot be represented.

Droid then turns the MCP tool into a model function named `Skillplane___skills_search`. The downstream function-schema validator doesn’t support that Unicode regex syntax, so it rejects the complete tool catalog with HTTP 400 before the model runs or any Skillplane tool is called.

That explains why it happened even though you wanted `pr-refetch-fix`: `skills_search` was merely present among the enabled tools. An incompatible schema can poison the whole request. The same `\p{L}\p{N}` failure has been reproduced in [another MCP client using a strict provider](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/60474). JSON Schema itself recommends ECMAScript regexes but warns that the full syntax is not widely supported; see its [regex portability guidance](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/regular_expressions).

There’s also a revealing compatibility gap in Skillplane: its Linear-specific catalog already strips `pattern`, but generic OAuth clients—including Factory—receive it unchanged in [index.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane/mcp/src/index.ts:173).

The best fix is on Skillplane’s side:

- Omit this `pattern` from the model-facing MCP schema.
- Keep the Unicode validation server-side; it already exists independently in [domain search validation](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/experiments/skillplane/packages/domain/src/search.ts:207).
- Alternatively, replace it with `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$`, but that would intentionally reject non-Latin tags.

A temporary Factory workaround is to disable only `skills_search` in its MCP configuration and use `workspaces_list` → `skills_list` → `skill_retrieve`. Factory documents `disabledTools` in its [MCP configuration guide](https://docs.factory.ai/harness/mcp).

So, in one line: **Skillplane publishes a standards-oriented but poorly portable Unicode regex, and Factory’s downstream function-schema validator rejects it before Droid can do any work.**
